title: Test a fetch-level abort by stubbing global.fetch, not fetchAPI
answers: how do I unit test an aborted request in the MLflow JS UI
how to test that a timeout actually cancels the fetch
why do my fetchAPI mock tests pass when the signal is dropped
how to fake timers for a React Query request timeout
body:
Stub global.fetch with a jest.fn that rejects with new DOMException('Aborted', 'AbortError') when init.signal fires 'abort'. Do not mock fetchAPI. fetchAPI must forward signal into the RequestInit it builds, and a mock hides that passthrough. In the PR, removing the ...restOptions spread made the change inert in a browser while all fetchAPI-mocked tests stayed green.
Use jest.useFakeTimers() and jest.advanceTimersByTime(SERVER_INFO_TIMEOUT_MS) to fire the deadline.
To check the timer, find the setTimeout spy call whose delay equals SERVER_INFO_TIMEOUT_MS and assert clearTimeout was called with its return value. Do not count pending timers, because React Query schedules its own.
Build the QueryClient with retry: false so failures are not retried.
applies: Jest tests in mlflow/server/js for code that passes signal or timeouts to fetch.
says: The server status request in the web console hangs indefinitely instead of timing out.
The experiment tracking interface continues waiting on stuck network calls without canceling them.
Server information queries keep retrying automatically after failing from a connection timeout.
Ensure slow backend status checks are aborted when the response deadline passes.
search: Unit testing fetch-level aborts in Jest requires stubbing global.fetch to reject with an AbortError DOMException rather than mocking fetchAPI. Applies to tests in mlflow/server/js where fetchAPI must forward the signal into RequestInit without mocks hiding broken passthroughs. Use jest.useFakeTimers() and jest.advanceTimersByTime(SERVER_INFO_TIMEOUT_MS), assert clearTimeout was called on the matching setTimeout spy call, do not count pending timers due to React Query, and initialize QueryClient with retry: false.
